I was wondering if anyone could offer some knowledgeable advice on what a good alternative would be to switch up for the RDL's? Here is what my leg/ab day looks like

Quads

  • Leg Press

Hamstrings

  • Romanian Deadlift

abs

I never feel great about my RDL form but I watch in the mirror and my back isn't arched and it's tight and my friends say it looks fine so I don't worry too much. The only other hamstring exercises I would recommend are already on your list, although I guess you could do dumbbell lunges. I'm not a fan of those myself.

Yeah, I tried searching for alternatives, but a lot of people recommended lying leg curls, which I'm already doing. I can really feel the burn in my target areas with the other workouts. The RDL feels strenuous in the wrong areas, but I'm wondering if it is just because I'm slightly out of shape. If I can't find an alternative, I'm going to keep practicing form with my brook until leg day next week.
You're doing a lot of accessory lifts. Focusing on squat and rdl is always better than accessories. If you're not a fan of Romanians I typically recommend single leg curls or lunges.

You've got the main alternatives covered so I'd suggest a variation. The Dead Start variation starts halfway through the rep, adding a new twist to the exercise.

How to:

Place a dumbbell on a slightly elevated surface, like a stepper, in front of you.

Bend over as if performing a Single-Arm, Single-Leg RDL, grasp the dumbbell and perform a full rep, starting from the bottom position.

Lower the weight back to the stepper and repeat.

I'm sure other will say it too, if your worried about your form ask someone to talk you through the rep and keep you in tuned with your form, coaching queues etc. If that fails lift beside a mirror.

Since you're already working the hamstrings with knee flexion exercises, I would recommend a hip extension replacement. While this will shift focus to the glutes for the exercise, the hamstrings would still be recruited in the movement in a natural range of motion. Also, RDL's are similarly more hip extension, so such exercises would be closer replacements. Off the top of my head, you could do weighted bridges or hyperextensions (except while maintaining a flat back and focusing on hip hinge). If you're up for something closer to a deadlift, you can try one-legged RDL's with dumbbells. It'll force you to use less weight and work on your balance more, but many people find the motion to be more natural (if you lift a leg when you bend over to pick something up, you're performing the basics of the motion).
